main_body: half-timbered barn/farm building with tiled roof and central dormer
top_band: tiled roof slope from row 0 to row 53 (with a central dormer interrupts rows 15-48)
evidence: The building clearly shows a large foreshortened tiled roof slope (rows 0-53) sitting above a vertical south wall (rows 54-88). Below the roof edge (row 53), there is a dark eave overhang shadow along rows 54-57 on the plaster wall, and the double barn doors and windows are visibly inset with dark framing and inner shadows.

style.evidence: The candidate matches the Beodeul reference buildings directly in tile work, plaster grain, and timber shading. The roof uses the exact 5-6 step terracotta/purple-brown tile pattern with bright ridge highlights, the plaster walls have subtle multi-tone speckle, and the wooden doors and beams use rich multi-step brown ramps and dark brown material outlines.
